banding_map — 2D gray op

• Data kinds: image → image

Usage

Returns where tonal steps (banding) are visible. a is the bit count; b is the window.

A step becomes "visible" when 3 conditions hold together, and this op multiplies those 3 in turn.

1. It sits on the step grid — the value lies on the grid k*Δ. An image that has not been quantized has no banding (floating-point noise is dropped here).

2. The window moves by exactly 1 step — the difference between maximum and minimum in the window (peak-to-peak) is 1 times Δ. Neither 0 times (flat) nor 2 times or more (a real contour).

3. It is a sparse line — steps appear as thin lines along contour lines. If a wide area responds all at once, it is not a step but dithering or a fine pattern.

a is the quantization bit count 1-8 (if the input is already quantized, give its level count). b is the window size (3-9 pixels).

Why these 3 stages (measured): judging by peak-to-peak alone, white noise flagged 41.7 % of pixels and an ordered-dithered image 97.7 % as "steps" — because the local ptp merely happening to equal Δ satisfies the condition. Condition 1 drops the noise and condition 3 drops the dithering. On a gradient quantized to 3-bit, 7.0 % (the step lines themselves) remains.

Conditions of use: (1) If the input bit count is wrong it has no effect at all — when unsure, measure it first with effective_bit_depth. (2) If the input has ever been smoothly interpolated or resampled, condition 1 breaks (it leaves the grid). To measure steps, apply it to the image right after quantization.
